newsitem.title: UK: Unilever to cut 150 jobs in UK.
newsitem.headline: Unilever to cut 150 jobs in UK.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch conglomerate Unilever Plc said on Tuesday it will close its unit based in Bristol, southwest England, with the loss of 150 jobs.
The unit traditionally concentrated in developing markets for products such as tea and detergents in countries where Unilever had little presence.
However, that role had been overtaken by newly-formed specialist regional groups, a company spokesman said.

"As the global economy continues to grow, it is clear that our business in Bristol cannot continue to develop markets as efficiently as the regional groups which are close to local consumers," chairman David Stevenson said in a statement.

Some 190 people were employed at Unilever International in Bristol, and 150 people would be made redundant in phases from September 1997, the spokesman said. The office would close in June next year and the remaining 40 people would be redeployed within Unilever.
